The overview

Medellin is Colombia's reinvented "City of Eternal Spring" — a green Andean valley city with near-perfect weather year-round, gondolas climbing the hillsides, flower-filled plazas and one of Latin America's most remarkable urban comeback stories.

Top things to do in Medellin

  • Ride the Metrocable gondolas over the hillside barrios
  • Tour transformed Comuna 13 with its escalators and street art
  • Stroll Plaza Botero and the Botero sculptures
  • Day-trip to El Penol rock and colorful Guatape
  • Wander El Poblado's cafes, restaurants and nightlife

Best time to visit

The sweet spot for Medellin is generally year-round — and the cheapest fares often land just outside peak season.

Is it safe?

Check your government's latest travel advisory. Watch your belongings in crowds and tourist areas, and check your government’s current advisory before you go. Visa for US passports: Check entry requirements for US passports.

A bit of history

Founded in 1616 and long an industrial and coffee-trade hub, Medellin became infamous for cartel violence in the 1980s-90s, then engineered a celebrated turnaround with bold public transit, libraries and parks that made it a global model for urban renewal.

Culture & language

Paisa culture is proud, entrepreneurial and warm — sweeping mountain views, the hearty bandeja paisa, salsa and reggaeton (the city birthed global stars), and a spring-like climate that keeps life outdoors all year.

Language: the local language · English spoken: varies
